title: Delivering defined amounts of purified protein with high precision into living cells
protocol: Optimize electroporation conditions for the cell line using an inert fluorescent standard like dextran.
Co-load cells with the protein of interest and dextran after optimizing electroporation parameters.
Label the protein of interest for increased delivery quantification possibilities.
Establish electroporation efficiency by labeling cells with antibodies against the protein if it is unlabeled.
Maintain a consistent volume of electroporation buffer across different protein concentrations.
Take cell culture media and a 6-well plate with laminin-coated coverslips out of the incubator.
Under sterile conditions, remove DPBS from each well.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed media to each well of the 6-well plate.
Place the plate back in the incubator.
Thaw dextran or protein on ice in the dark.
If delivering protein, preclarify by centrifugation at >100,000 × g for 20 minutes to remove aggregates.
Harvest cells from three 60%-80% confluent 10 cm dishes using trypsinization (1.5 mL total).
Inhibit trypsin with 8% FBS in DMEM/F12 media (6 mL total).
Combine harvested cells into one 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 150 × g for 3 minutes to remove trypsin.
Wash the cell pellet twice in DPBS, carefully resuspending the pellet each time.
Remove the 6-well plate from the incubator.
Add dextran/protein to the total electroporation volume.
Remove DPBS from the sample.
Resuspend pellet gently in a minimal amount of electroporation buffer R.
Add an additional 10 μL cell suspension for potential arcing, and another 10 μL each for counting cells and as a non-electroporation control.
Mix the cell suspension to ensure even distribution.
Use 10 μL of cell volume to count cells; aim for a range of 3–5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Dilute in buffer R if the cell count is too high.
Add 10 μL of total cell suspension volume to each Eppendorf tube using a 20 μL pipette tip.
Stir and mix the solution gently, avoiding bubble formation.
Draw the solution into one 10 μL Neon Pipette Tip (Thermo Fisher).
Invert the pipette tip to check for air bubbles; if present, dispense back into the Eppendorf tube and redraw or pulse centrifuge and resuspend.
Use one single 1,400 v 20 ms pulse for electroporation.
Dispense the contents of the pipette tip into a 6 well plate with coverslips and media after completion of the pulse.
Change the Neon Pipette Tip (Thermo Fisher) between different conditions.
Place 6 well plate in an incubator (37°C, 5% CO2) for 2 hours to allow cells to adhere.
Plate a non-electroporated control from the total cell suspension volume simultaneously with electroporated samples.
Prepare 6 mL of 4% PFA in PBS from 16% paraformaldehyde by adding 1.5 mL of cold 16% PFA to 4.5 mL of PBS.
Remove cells from incubator after 2 hours and confirm adherence by light microscopy.
Quickly aspirate the media and add 1 mL of 4% PFA per well for fixation.
Fix cells for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Remove PFA and safely dispose of it.
Dispense PBS liberally into each well to cover the cells.
Remove PBS and gently add more to remove traces of PFA.
Repeat PBS washing once.
Leave PBS in wells for 5 minutes in the dark.
Label and prepare slide (25 × 75 mm, Superfrost).
Invert a bottle of ProLong Diamond Antifade mounting media and dispense one large drop.
Tilt the 6 well plate.
Use forceps to carefully grab each coverslip.
Keep track of which face the cells are adhered to.
Gently drain the coverslip of excess PBS through capillary action by touching the edge close to a KimWipe or absorbent towel, being careful not to touch the cell-covered face.
Place each coverslip on the mounting media so that cells are facing down toward the slide.
Keep slides in the dark and undisturbed for 48 h.
Seal slides with a minimal amount of clear nail polish after 48 h.
Allow the nail polish to dry completely before imaging.
Use the EVOS XL digital inverted microscope equipped with the 20× 0.5 NA objective to measure efficiency.
Locate a field of view in the transmitted light channel, then focus and capture an image.
Without changing the field of view, switch to the fluorescence channel and capture another image.
Repeat and save images in tiff format.
Count manually by dividing the total number of cells (transmitted light channel) by the number of fluorescent cells.
Binarize each image using Process/Binary/Make Binary.
Erode the binarized image using Process/Binary/Erode until cells appear whole.
Convert the binarized image to a mask using Process/Binary/Convert to mask.
Analyze particles under “Show” select “Outlines.”
Limit cell size by selecting a threshold number (for example 10-Infinity).
Count cells using results generated in Analyze Particles for both the light and fluorescence channels.
Use the EVOS XL digital inverted microscope equipped with the 20× 0.5 NA objective to measure fluorescence intensity.
Select settings for both light intensity and exposure time that provide good signal for both high and low fluorescence intensity cells.
Ensure highly fluorescent cells do not saturate the signal while retaining good signal-to-noise ratio for lower intensity cells.
Increase exposure time over light power to reduce bleaching.
Perform measurements for both channels.
Locate cells suitable for single-cell measurements.
Center the cells in the field of view.
Focus on the centered cells.
Capture the image of the focused cells.
Ensure cells are not touching other cells.
Do not change imaging settings once established.
Perform all imaging for each biological replicate on the same day.
Use identical imaging parameters for consistency.
Capture images for 30–40 cells.
Save captured images in tiff format.
Open Fiji software to analyze images.
Import all images from one data set as an image sequence.
Create one maximum intensity Z-projection of the image sequence.
Select an area devoid of cells or signal on the maximum intensity Z-projection.
Adjust the brightness and contrast by reducing the maximum intensity.
Draw a small rectangle in the selected area using the rectangle tool.
While holding down shift, identify another area free of cells/signal to draw another box.
Measure the mean intensity of the background for each image.
Manually subtract the measured background value from the image.
Alternatively, select the window for the image sequence.
Restore the selection by pressing Shift + E or selecting Edit/Selection/Restore Selection.
Transfer the drawn boxes to the image sequence.
Ensure every box represents an area devoid of cells on each image in the sequence.
Download the background subtraction macro from the specified location.
Run the background subtraction macro.
For simultaneous measurement of two channels, subtract the background for each channel separately.
Use the brighter channel to locate and threshold the cell boundary.
Transfer the selection from one channel to the other using Shift + E or Edit/Selection/Restore Selection.
In the “Set Measurements” window, select Area, Integrated Density, Mean Gray Value, and Median.
Ensure that both fluorescence channels have identical area measurements per cell when measuring two channels.
Check images in the sequence to ensure background subtraction was performed correctly.
Draw a box in an area devoid of cells to verify background subtraction.
Take a measurement by selecting Ctrl + M or Analyze/Measure.
Check the mean value to establish signal-to-noise ratio.
Select both an area for background and a cell to determine signal-to-noise ratio accurately.
Threshold the signal using Image/Adjust/Threshold to optimize cell selection.
Optimize the thresholding so that cells are selected without including background noise.
If background subtraction was done correctly, ensure the signal-to-noise ratio is high.
Use the wand tool located in the toolbar to select an individual cell.
Measure the selected cell by pressing Ctrl + M or selecting Analyze/Measure.
Utilize the ROI Manager (Analyze/Tools/ROI Manager) to measure cells and save analysis records.
Assess protein delivery by performing immunostaining using an antibody specific for that protein if it is unlabeled.
Electroporate cells where the gene encoding the protein of interest is knocked out to assess electroporation efficiency.
Alternatively, add an epitope tag to the electroporated protein.
Ensure antibodies used in immunolabeling experiments are specifically interacting with their intended targets.
Indirectly assess protein delivery by co-electroporating a fluorescent dextran similar in size to the protein being introduced.
Pre-warm 10 mL aliquot of media (DMEM/F-12 with 10% FBS) in an incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
Divide 5 mL among six 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Thaw Alexa647-tagged Thymosin β4 or your choice of high quality fluorescently tagged protein or molecule.
Follow the protocol of step 1 with 2–3 times the starting cell volume (6–9 60%–80% confluent 10 cm dishes).
Double the electroporation volumes for four electroporations/condition instead of two.
Thoroughly resuspend the total cell volume.
Aliquot the total cell volume equally among all conditions.
Mix fluorescently tagged protein with lysate to create a control without electroporation.
Electroporate cells according to the protocol.
Deliver electroporated cells into Eppendorf tubes and partially close the lids for gas exchange.
Allow cells to rest for 10 min in an incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
Centrifuge Eppendorf tubes at 150 × g for 3 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove media from the centrifuged samples.
Replace removed media with 1 mL of DPBS, gently resuspending the pellet.
Repeat the process of centrifugation, gentle re-suspension, and washing in DPBS three times.
Leave the final pellet suspended in DPBS.
Suspend each pellet in a fluorometry-suitable protein buffer in the same volume.
Select the “Fluorometer” function on a Qubit 4 Fluorometer or equivalent instrument.
Choose the Red (635 nm) excitation wavelength for measurement.
Record relative fluorescence units for each sample.
Graph the recorded fluorescence as a function of protein concentration in the electroporation chamber.
Dispense 4–5 mL/dish of cell culture media (DMEM/F-12 with 10% FBS) in six 60 mm tissue culture dishes and place dishes in an incubator for a minimum of 30 min prior to electroporation.
Pre-warm a 50 mL aliquot of media to 37°C in a water or bead bath.
Make a 2 mL RIPA buffer solution with 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 1% Triton X-100, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate, and 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulfate.
Add 80 μL of solubilized 25× Roche Protease inhibitor cocktail to the RIPA buffer solution.
Keep the RIPA buffer on ice.
Aliquot 10 mL of DPBS and keep it on ice.
Label 12 Eppendorf tubes and keep them on ice.
Pre-chill a microcentrifuge capable of speeds up to 10,000 × g to 4°C.
Aspirate media from the cells on ice and rinse with ice-cold DPBS.
Replace DPBS with 250 μL of RIPA buffer.
Incubate cells on ice with RIPA buffer for 5 min.
Collect cells using a cell scraper by tilting the dish.
Transfer the RIPA buffer solution with cells to a chilled, labeled Eppendorf tube using a 1 mL pipette.
Repeat harvesting and transferring for all plates.
Generate whole cell lysates by mechanical lysis of cells through repeated passage (5×) through a 27G needle on ice.
Centrifuge lysate at 10,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Prepare 6× SDS buffer with Orange G for Li-Cor system storage between 20°C and 25°C.
Add 12.5 μL of β-mercaptoethanol to 237.5 μL of 6× SDS buffer during centrifugation step.
Take 30 μL of lysate from each sample for protein quantification.
Load 10 μL of each sample into three wells on a 96 well plate for protein quantification.
Transfer 145 μL of lysate to Eppendorf tubes labeled in step diii.
Dilute transferred samples with 30 μL of prepared 6× SDS buffer.
Keep all samples on ice until loading.
Take a 96 well plate and load BSA standards.
Dispense 10 μL of each sample into three wells for protein quantification.
Add 190 μL of BCA reagent to all wells using a multi-channel pipette.
Incubate the 96 well plate with BCA working reagent at 37°C for a minimum of 30 minutes.
Read absorbance values from the 96 well plate with a plate reader.
Denature samples at 95°C for 5 minutes in a heating block.
Store denatured samples directly on ice after heat treatment.
Centrifuge samples (5 minutes, 5,000 × g, 4°C) following storage on ice.
Make 1× running buffer by combining 1.44% glycine, 0.3% tris base, and 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS).
Prepare 1× transfer buffer with 7.5% glycine and 1.21% tris base, adding 20% methanol last.
Store transfer buffer aliquots at -20°C for future use.
Load the gel in an XCell SureLock Mini-Cell Electrophoresis system or equivalent device.
Prepare a Novex tris-glycine 1.0 mm mini gel for SDS-PAGE.
In 1× running buffer, load 10 μL of WesternSure Pre-Stained Chemiluminescent Protein Ladder into the left-most lane.
Load 10 μg of each sample into subsequent lanes, keeping track of which lanes receive which samples.
Load empty lanes with 2 μL of 6× SDS buffer.
Run gel at constant voltage (approximately 2 hours, 120 V at 20°C–25°C) until the loading dye reaches close to the bottom of the gel.
Wet a polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) membrane in methanol for 1 minute to activate it.
Dispose of used methanol safely.
Rinse the activated PVDF membrane twice with de-ionized water, shaking the second rinse for 2 minutes.
Transfer the membrane into transfer buffer and ensure it does not dry out while on an orbital shaker or rocker.
Pre-wet filter pads, blotting paper, and gel in ice-cold transfer buffer.
Assemble stack for transfer: place filter pad, blotting paper, gel, membrane, blotting paper, and filter pad from bottom to top.
Transfer on ice at constant current using PVDF membrane (50 min, 100 mA).
Rinse the membrane twice in distilled water.
Block membrane for 15 minutes in 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in tris buffered saline (TBS) at room temperature.
Dilute primary antibodies in 5% BSA with 0.1% Tween-20 and add to membrane.
Incubate primary antibody while shaking overnight at 4°C.
Wash the membrane three times for 30 minutes each in TBS containing 0.1% Tween-20.
Incubate membrane with Li-Cor secondary antibodies diluted in 5% BSA, 0.1% Tween-20, and TBS for two hours at room temperature while shaking.
Wash the membrane three times for 30 minutes each in TBS containing 0.1% Tween-20.
Wash the membrane twice in 1× TBS.
Visualize western bands according to manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify the bands according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Use a quantitative western analysis such as via the Li-Cor system to maintain linearity in detection.
Perform quantitative western blotting to determine how much protein is delivered in reference to endogenous levels.
If establishing intracellular concentrations is desired, load a range of purified protein concentrations to generate a standard curve.
Calculate concentration of protein per cell from western blot results using both the cell volume and the number of cells loaded per well.
